newsitem.title: LATVIA: AIR BALTIC PLANS BREAK EVEN ON '97 FLIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: AIR BALTIC PLANS BREAK EVEN ON '97 FLIGHTS.

text.p: Latvia's Air Baltic said on Monday that it hoped to break even on operating flights in 1997.

"In 1997, we plan to break even in our operating flights, while the investment programme continues in 1997 and in the first half of 1998," Oleg Korshe, Air Baltic's Senior Vice President, told Reuters.
The company has not revealed any profit or loss figures since coming into existence in late 1995, but has said it made a loss in its first year of business.
He added that the company's passenger turnover is expected to grow to 170,000 in 1997 from a 115,000 in 1996.
"The aim of 1996 was to create a western-style air carrier, and this aim was completed," he said.
"We are not planning much in terms of new flights this year, but we keep in mind Moscow and St. Petersburg," he said.
"We are going to optimize existing routes in order to get the most out of them," he added.
Air Baltic, which is nearly a third owned by Scandinavian Airlines , was formed from Latvia's old state airline and the government owns 51 percent.
SAS has 29 percent and Swedfund and the Danish Investment Fund also own stakes.
